subject: Dedicated sizing conflict: Zenova vs HeliosCloud — prioritization needed
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing shortfall — Zenova & HeliosCloud overlap (need prioritization)

Team,

Quick summary: our capacity planner flagged a sustained GPU shortfall in the us-west-2 dedicated pool for the Oct–Dec window. Two deals with overlapping start dates and size expectations are the primary drivers: Zenova (pilot → prod ramp, requesting ~8 A100-equivalent slots initially) and HeliosCloud (reserved 12-slot commit for Q4). If both land as contracted we exceed the pool by ~20–25% during peak hours.

Attached: capacity heatmap and the Zenova mutual action plan.

As this will materially impact SLA targets and margin math, we need a short, defendable prioritization rule set to take to sales and the customers. Options I see:
- Enforce SLA-first: customer with SLA-backed committed reserved capacity (HeliosCloud) gets priority.
- Deal-weighted: prioritize by ARR + expansion potential (Zenova has higher expansion upside but currently smaller commit).
- Hybrid tranche: carve a conservative guaranteed slice and allow burstable pool for ramping customers with negotiated limits.

Please reply with recommended approach and any constraints I should surface to finance/ops before we loop the sellers and customers. I want a decision to present to Elena (Zenova) and Samir (HeliosCloud) by COB Monday.

-David

--
David Kim
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing shortfall — Zenova & HeliosCloud overlap (need prioritization)

David —

Thanks for the ping. I ran a quick simulation (attached spreadsheet) with three scenarios: strict-reserve (favor existing reserved deals), ramp-favor (give Zenova a 6-slot ramp window for 4 weeks then evaluate), and split-tranche (50/50 guaranteed + burst). My read: split-tranche smooths customer experience and preserves our unit economics if we gate burst with a telemetry-based throttle. It also keeps Zenova engaged while preserving HeliosCloud's SLA baseline.

Operational constraints: we cannot fragment a single customer's reserved pool across >2 physical racks without telecom & infra approvals — that caps how much 'burst' we can promise regionally. Also need legal to sign off on burst billing terms.

Recommend: propose split-tranche to customers as a compromise, with a 30-day evaluation clause and explicit burst throttles. If sales push back, escalate to leadership for carve-out.

-Ben

Attachment: 20260822_capacity-heatmap.xlsx (sheets: scenarios, assumptions, rack-mapping)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing shortfall — Zenova & HeliosCloud overlap (need prioritization)

Ben — appreciate the scenarios. A couple of product/contract considerations to add:

1) HeliosCloud's PO already has a committed start date and SLAs tied to latency percentiles for inference — that gives them contractual precedence unless the deal explicitly contains a force-majeure / capacity carve-out.
2) Zenova is early-stage but has indicated a high-velocity roadmap; redelivering an underwhelming ramp could jeopardize long-term expansion and referenceability.
3) Recommend we build a three-criteria decision matrix: (a) contractually-committed SLA, (b) near-term ARR impact if delayed, (c) technical risk of moving workloads (migration/region constraints). Score both deals and use threshold-based rules to recommend yes/no for carve.

If the matrix still ties, leadership should weigh strategic account prioritization (reference value) vs. contractual risk. Happy to draft the matrix this weekend.

-Laura

--
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 13:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing shortfall — Zenova & HeliosCloud overlap (need prioritization)

Looping in the commercial leads and legal early will reduce churn. I propose we:
- Share the split-tranche proposal with both accounts as a short-term operational mitigation.
- Include explicit billing language for burst (per-GPU-minute at surge rate) and an automatic capping rule tied to telemetry (95th percentile requests).
- If HeliosCloud insists on guaranteed full capacity, escalate to Sales Leadership for contract remedies (credits/compensation if we reassign).

I will draft the customer-facing note and the contract clause. David — can you confirm which racks and AZs are non-negotiable for HeliosCloud? That affects our ability to split.

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rojas <elena@zenova.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@helioscloud.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Dedicated sizing shortfall — proposed mitigation (split-tranche)

Elena / Samir —

Following internal review, attached is a proposed short-term mitigation for the Oct–Dec window: a split-tranche arrangement where each account has a guaranteed minimum (HeliosCloud: 9 slots guaranteed; Zenova: 5 slots guaranteed) plus a shared burst pool (8 slots) with telemetry-based throttles. Bursts will be billed at the published surge rate; we'll enforce max sustained burst per account to avoid noisy neighbors.

Key notes:
- This is a temporary arrangement for Q4 only; we will re-evaluate after a 30-day ramp window.
- If HeliosCloud requires the full reserved capacity guaranteed, we need to escalate contract terms; that could trigger credits or require us to buy additional capacity (both options are on the table).
- Attached: mutual action plan (Zenova_v2) and the capacity heatmap for the region.

Please reply with any redlines or acceptance by EOD Tuesday so we can finalize the billing/legal language.

-David

Attachments: zenova_mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf
From: Elena Rojas <elena@zenova.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Dedicated sizing shortfall — proposed mitigation (split-tranche)

David —

Thanks for the quick response and the proposal. Zenova is open to a guaranteed ramp + burst, but two asks: (1) can burst be applied across additional regions (we have a small presence in us-east-1) to reduce contention, and (2) can you provide a firm timeline for when the 30-day evaluation metrics will be published (we need clear KPIs to make go/no-go decisions on our side).

If those two items are addressed, we can accept the temporary arrangement while legal finalizes the amended MSA.

Best,
Elena Rojas
Head of Ops, Zenova
